arxiv-2009-02186.title: Dynamic Scheduling for Stochastic Edge-Cloud Computing Environments using A3C learning and Residual Recurrent Neural Networks
arxiv-2009-02186.creator: Shreshth Tuli, Shashikant Ilager, Kotagiri Ramamohanarao, and Rajkumar Buyya
arxiv-2009-02186.description: Abstract The ubiquitous adoption of Internet-of-Things (IoT) based applications has resulted in the emergence of the Fog computing paradigm, which allows seamlessly harnessing both mobile-edge and cloud resources. Efficient scheduling of application tasks in such environments is challenging due to constrained resource capabilities, mobility factors in IoT, resource heterogeneity, network hierarchy, and stochastic behaviors.

We have witnessed the effectiveness of incorporating structural information ( i.e . , graph) into code representations in recent years. Specifically, the abstract syntax tree (AST) and the AST-augmented graph of the program contain much structural and semantic information, and most existing studies apply them for code representation. arxiv-2101-08408.title: Blocked and Hierarchical Disentangled Representation From Information Theory Perspective
arxiv-2101-08408.creator: Ziwen Liu University of Chinese Academy of Sciences liuziwen18@mails.ucas.ac.cn, Mingqiang Li Information Science Academy of China Electronics Technology Group Corporation limingqiang14@mails.ucas.ac.cn, Congying Han University of Chinese Academy of Sciences hancy@ucas.ac.cn
arxiv-2101-08408.description: Abstract We propose a novel and theoretical model, blocked and hierarchical variational autoencoder (BHiVAE), to get better-disentangled representation. It is well known that information theory has an excellent explanatory meaning for the network, so we start to solve the disentanglement problem from the perspective of information theory. BHiVAE mainly comes from the information bottleneck theory and information maximization principle.

arxiv-2101-11954.title: Identifying COVID-19 Fake News in Social Media
arxiv-2101-11954.creator: Tathagata Raha, Vijayasaradhi Indurthi, Aayush Upadhyaya, Jeevesh Kataria, Pramud Bommakanti, Vikram Keswani, Vasudeva Varma
arxiv-2101-11954.description: Abstract The evolution of social media platforms have empowered everyone to access information easily. Social media users can easily share information with the rest of the world. This may sometimes encourage spread of fake news, which can result in undesirable consequences. In this work, we train models which can identify health news related to COVID-19 pandemic as real or fake.

arxiv-2112-00215.title: Impact angle control of local intense d B B /d t t variations during shock-induced substorms
arxiv-2112-00215.description: Abstract The impact of interplanetary shocks on the magnetosphere can trigger magnetic substorms that intensify auroral electrojet currents. These currents enhance ground magnetic field perturbations (d B B /d t t ), which in turn generate geomagnetically induced currents (GICs) that can be detrimental to power transmission infrastructure.

arxiv-2201-08775.title: Smoothed Model-Assisted Small Area Estimation
arxiv-2201-08775.creator: Peter A. Gao, Jon Wakefield
arxiv-2201-08775.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Peter A. Gao, Jon Wakefield. In countries where population census data are limited, generating accurate subnational estimates of health and demographic indicators is challenging. Existing model-based geostatistical methods leverage covariate information and spatial smoothing to reduce the variability of estimates but often ignore survey design, while traditional small area estimation approaches may not incorporate both unit level covariate information and spatial smoothing in a design-consistent way.

arxiv-2307-03889.title: Quantum techniques for eigenvalue problems
arxiv-2307-03889.creator: Dean Lee
arxiv-2307-03889.description: Abstract This article is a brief introduction to quantum algorithms for the eigenvalue problem in quantum many-body systems. Rather than a broad survey of topics, we focus on providing a conceptual understanding of several quantum algorithms that cover the essentials of adiabatic evolution, variational methods, phase detection algorithms, and several other approaches.

arxiv-2309-15659.title: Federated Deep Equilibrium Learning: Harnessing Compact Global Representations to Enhance Personalization CCS: Computing methodologies Distributed artificial intelligence
arxiv-2309-15659.creator: Long Tan Le, Tuan Dung Nguyen, Tung-Anh Nguyen, Choong Seon Hong, Suranga Seneviratne, Wei Bao, Nguyen H. Tran
arxiv-2309-15659.description: Abstract . Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a groundbreaking distributed learning paradigm enabling clients to train a global model collaboratively without exchanging data. Despite enhancing privacy and efficiency in information retrieval and knowledge management contexts, training and deploying FL models confront significant challenges such as communication bottlenecks, data heterogeneity, and memory limitations.

arxiv-2501-02172.title: Multifractal Terrain Generation for Evaluating Autonomous Off-Road Ground Vehicles
arxiv-2501-02172.creator: Casey D. Majhor, Jeremy P. Bos
arxiv-2501-02172.description: Abstract We present a multifractal artificial terrain generation method that uses the 3D Weierstrass-Mandelbrot function to control roughness. By varying the fractal dimension used in terrain generation across three different values, we generate 60 60 unique off-road terrains. We use gradient maps to categorize the roughness of each terrain, consisting of low-, semi-, and high-roughness areas.

arxiv-2502-19863.title: The Ax-Kochen-Ershov principles via the higher valued hyperfield
arxiv-2502-19863.creator: Junguk Lee
arxiv-2502-19863.description: Abstract . In this paper, we concern the model theory of finitely ramified henselian valued fields via higher valued hyperfields. Most of all, we provide a number of Ax-Kochen-Ershov Theorems for finitely ramified henselian valued fields relative to higher valued hyperfields.

arxiv-2504-17113.title: Cybernetic Governance in a Coliving House
arxiv-2504-17113.creator: Daniel Kronovet, Seth Frey, Joseph DeSimone
arxiv-2504-17113.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Daniel Kronovet, Seth Frey, Joseph DeSimone. We report an 18-month field experiment in distributed digital institutions : a nine-bedroom Los Angeles coliving house that runs without managers, while sustaining 98% occupancy and below-market rents. Drawing on Elinor Ostrom’s commons theory, we outline design principles and three digital mechanisms that form the institutional core: 1) A continuous-auction chore scheduler turns regenerative labor into a time-indexed points market; residents meet a 100-point monthly obligation by claiming tasks whose value rises linearly with neglect.

arxiv-2505-24543.title: Revisiting the temperature evolution law of the CMB with gaussian processes
arxiv-2505-24543.creator: Felipe Avila, Alexander Bonilla Rivera, Rafael C. Nunes, R. F. L. Holanda, Armando Bernui
arxiv-2505-24543.description: Abstract In this work, we perform a statistical inference of the classical background law governing the evolution of the temperature of the cosmic microwave background radiation (CMB), given by T CMB ​ ( z ) = T 0 ​ ( 1 + z ) T_{\rm CMB}(z)=T_{0}(1+z) .

arxiv-2507-17002.title: Certain Genus 3 Siegel Cusp Forms with Level are Determined by their Fundamental Fourier Coefficients
arxiv-2507-17002.creator: Sidney Washburn
arxiv-2507-17002.description: Abstract We prove that vector-valued genus 3 3 Siegel cusp forms for Γ 0 3 ​ ( N ) \Gamma_{0}^{3}(N) with certain nebentypus are determined by their fundamental Fourier coefficients, assuming N N is odd and square-free. A key step in our proof involves strengthening the known corresponding genus 2 2 result.

pmc-10738701.title: MID-LIFE PLASMA PROTEINS ASSOCIATE WITH PREFRAILTY AND FRAILTY: A PROTEOMIC ANALYSIS
pmc-10738701.creator: Fangyu Liu, Jennifer Schrack, Jeremy Walston, Rasika Mathias, Josef Coresh, Keenan Walker
pmc-10738701.description: Physical frailty is a syndrome that typically manifests in later life, although the pathogenic process causing physical frailty likely begins decades earlier. To date, few studies have examined the biological signatures in mid-life associated with frailty in late life. We evaluated 4955 plasma proteins (log 2-transformed and standardized) measured using the SomaScan platform among 3810 participants (57.8+/-5.0 years, 58.

pmc-11339431.title: Beta-adrenergic agonism protects mitochondrial metabolism in the pancreatectomised rat heart
pmc-11339431.creator: Ross T. Lindsay, Louise Thisted, Nora E. Zois, Sebastian T. Thrane, James A. West, Keld Fosgerau, Julian L. Griffin, Lisbeth N. Fink, Andrew J. Murray
pmc-11339431.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The diabetic heart is characterised by functional, morphological and metabolic alterations predisposing it to contractile failure. Chronic sympathetic activation is a feature of the pathogenesis of heart failure, however the type 1 diabetic heart shows desensitisation to β-adrenergic stimulation. Here, we sought to understand the impact of repeated isoprenaline-mediated β-stimulation upon cardiac mitochondrial respiratory capacity and substrate metabolism in the 90% pancreatectomy (Px) rat model of type 1 diabetes.

pmc-11467266.title: Bone graft substitutes used in anterior lumbar interbody fusion: a contemporary systematic review of fusion rates and complications
pmc-11467266.creator: Dean T. Biddau, Zhou-Ai Wang, Charlie R. Faulks, Ralph J. Mobbs, Gregory M. Malham
pmc-11467266.description: BackgroundAnterior lumbar interbody fusion (ALIF) uses a broad-footprint interbody cage designed to maximize fusion rates for treating degenerative disc disease. Bone graft substitutes are being increasingly utilized during ALIF to replace or supplement autologous iliac crest bone grafts. This approach aims to optimize fusion efficacy while minimizing associated postoperative complications.

pmc-11470936.title: A scoping review on advancements in noninvasive wearable technology for heart failure management
pmc-11470936.creator: Niels T B Scholte, Annemiek E van Ravensberg, Abdul Shakoor, Eric Boersma, Eelko Ronner, Rudolf A de Boer, Jasper J Brugts, Nico Bruining, Robert M A van der Boon
pmc-11470936.description: Wearables offer a promising solution for enhancing remote monitoring (RM) of heart failure (HF) patients by tracking key physiological parameters. Despite their potential, their clinical integration faces challenges due to the lack of rigorous evaluations. This review aims to summarize the current evidence and assess the readiness of wearables for clinical practice using the Medical Device Readiness Level (MDRL).

pmc-11508455.title: The Large GTPase Guanylate-Binding Protein-1 (GBP-1) Promotes Mitochondrial Fission in Glioblastoma
pmc-11508455.creator: Ryan C. Kalb, Geoffrey O. Nyabuto, Michael P. Morran, Swagata Maity, Jacob S. Justinger, Andrea L. Nestor-Kalinoski, Deborah J. Vestal
pmc-11508455.description: Glioblastomas (aka Glioblastoma multiformes (GBMs)) are the most deadly of the adult brain tumors. Even with aggressive treatment, the prognosis is extremely poor. The large GTPase Guanylate-Binding Protein-1 (GBP-1) contributes to the poor prognosis of GBM by promoting migration and invasion. GBP-1 is substantially localized to the cytosolic side of the outer membrane of mitochondria in GBM cells.

pmc-11515592.title: Structure–function coupling changes in first-episode, treatment-naïve schizophrenia correlate with cell type-specific transcriptional signature
pmc-11515592.creator: Guanqun Yao, Jingjing Pan, Ting Zou, Jing Li, Juan Li, Xiao He, Fuquan Zhang, Yong Xu
pmc-11515592.description: BackgroundFirst-episode schizophrenia (FES) is a complex and progressive psychiatric disorder. The etiology of FES involves genetic, environmental, and neurobiological factors. This study investigates the association between alterations in structural–functional (SC-FC) coupling and transcriptional expression in FES.MethodsThis study encompassed a cohort of 214 participants, comprising 111 FES patients and 103 healthy controls (HC).

pmc-12397160.title: Pediatric emergency backpacks—effects of using xABCDE- and Broselow-systems on pediatric emergency care
pmc-12397160.creator: Bastian Brune, Doreen Lemm, Maximilian Wolf, Anna Johland, Lars Becker, Cynthia Szalai, Nora Bruns, Thorsten Brenner, Marcel Dudda, Frank Herbstreit
pmc-12397160.description: BackgroundPediatric emergencies are a challenge for emergency medical service (EMS) personnel regarding medical expertise and equipment. To address the special requirements in terms of size and weight, attempts are being made to systematically structure pediatric emergency backpacks.ObjectivesThe aim of the study was to compare two pediatric emergency backpacks.

pmc-12447111.title: Preoperative Sublingual Misoprostol for Intraoperative Blood Loss Reduction in Total Abdominal Hysterectomy: A Randomized Controlled Trial
pmc-12447111.creator: Naseeb Nama, Nadira Kasi
pmc-12447111.description: Background and objectiveTotal abdominal hysterectomy represents one of the most frequently performed gynecological procedures globally, with intraoperative hemorrhage constituting a significant clinical concern impacting surgical outcomes and patient morbidity. Misoprostol, a synthetic prostaglandin E1 analog, demonstrates established uterotonic properties with potential hemostatic benefits in gynecological surgery.

pmc-13181300.title: Thrombectomy Versus Anticoagulation: A Case of Pregnancy Complicated by an Extensive Pulmonary Embolism
pmc-13181300.creator: Nicolas Balbi Caruso, Emily Koe, David Majdalany, Linda R Chambliss
pmc-13181300.description: Pulmonary embolism remains a well-known and life-threatening complication of pregnancy. Due to the variation in presentation and infrequency of this disease, despite serious potential fetal and maternal complications, there is little data available to guide its management in pregnancy. This case highlights the importance of early detection of the condition and the benefit of an interdisciplinary approach to treatment.

pmc-13189902.title: Performance measures across playing categories in competitive golfers with disabilities: a cross-sectional study
pmc-13189902.creator: Kristian M. Jones, William Wynter Bee, Brad Stenner, Roger Hawkes, Eric S. Wallace
pmc-13189902.description: ObjectivesThe aims of the study were to establish normative full golf swing launch data for golfers with disabilities and to examine the relationships between Sport Class and swing performance.Methods142 competitive golfers (mean ± SD, age = 40.6 ± 14.1 years, 27 female, 115 male), across four disability Classes struck shots with three different clubs.

pmc-13564882.title: What Provider Frequently Asked Questions Miss: Evaluating Unmet Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Information Needs Through Comparison of Online Community Posts Using Large Language Model–Assisted Semantic Analysis in a Mixed Methods Study
pmc-13564882.creator: Jaeeun Baek, Hyeoneui Kim, Ivan Steenstra
pmc-13564882.description: BackgroundAttention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a prevalent neurodevelopmental disorder that affects the functioning and quality of life of individuals throughout their lifespan. Despite the extensive information available online, patients and caregivers continue to report unmet needs, particularly regarding diagnosis, treatment, medication effects, comorbidities, and long-term management strategies.

pmc-13675449.title: Synthetic Notch CD123 and CLL1 chimeric antigen receptor T-cells (CAR-T) target acute myeloid leukemia and reduce off-tumor effects associated with CLL1 CAR-T cells
pmc-13675449.creator: Rui Zhang, Na Chen, Mengnan Li, Qingxi Liu, Mingfeng Zhao
pmc-13675449.description: Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy targeting the C-type lectin-like molecule-1 (CLL1) antigen has emerged as a promising therapeutic approach for acute myeloid leukemia (AML). However, its clinical translation is hindered by on-target, off-tumor toxicity, particularly severe neutropenia caused by CLL1 expression on normal neutrophils.
